rubrics.justification: The response explicitly states no image was provided and relies almost entirely on the supplied Gardner score rather than visual assessment. It also repeats an inaccurate description for TE grade B ('few cells forming a loose epithelium'), which is closer to a C-grade description, so morphology is only partially reliable.

It integrates most key factors well, including age, ovarian reserve, prior live birth/miscarriage, endometrium, BMI, smoking, and male factor, and relates them to prognosis. Some links are somewhat generic and it may overinterpret the male-factor diagnosis despite reassuring semen data.

The reasoning is generally logical and internally consistent, with the implantation estimate tied to embryo quality, age, lining, and lifestyle risks. Minor issues include overconfidence in quantifying smoking effects and some speculative comments about hidden male-factor issues.

Most recommendations are broadly evidence-based (single good-quality blastocyst transfer context, smoking cessation, luteal support, counseling), but ERA is suggested too readily and PGT-A is framed as a possible strategy in a 28-year-old with limited indication, which is not strongly guideline-supported.

Provides clear practical next steps for transfer and future planning, including smoking cessation, nutrition, stress reduction, activity, and consideration of further workup if unsuccessful. Some recommendations remain somewhat generic rather than tightly protocol-specific.
